about: Pilot catalogue for the first vertical slice. Factual fields (year, runtime, credits) were compiled from general knowledge and are NOT yet verified against primary sources (source: editorial-seed). All 'terms' and 'advisories' are AI-assisted interpretations awaiting human review (source: ai-assisted-seed). Absent lengths are unknown, not zero. Book page counts are edition-dependent and deliberately omitted. 'advisories' lists only the categories that have been assessed; each value is an intensity, or [intensity, note] or [intensity, note, spoiler note]. 'ratings' are official ratings as [system, rating, reason], also unverified.

works.title: Arrival
works.summary: When mysterious vessels touch down around the world, a linguist is recruited to find a way to talk with whatever is inside them before fear outpaces understanding.

graphic-violence: A bombing and armed military standoffs; little is shown.

works.title: Solaris
works.summary: A psychologist travels to a research station orbiting an ocean planet to evaluate its exhausted crew, and finds the station haunted by presences drawn from their own pasts.

suicide-self-harm: Grief over a past suicide is central to the story.
A character attempts suicide by drinking liquid oxygen.

works.title: Stalker
works.summary: A guide leads a writer and a scientist into the Zone, a forbidden wilderness said to contain a room that grants a person's deepest wish.

works.title: Blade Runner
works.summary: In a rain-soaked future Los Angeles, a burned-out detective is called back to hunt down a group of fugitive artificial humans.

graphic-violence: Shootings and hand-to-hand fights, with some blood.
sexual-content: Brief nudity and a forceful romantic scene.

works.title: Blade Runner 2049
works.summary: Thirty years after the original, a new blade runner uncovers a buried secret that could upend what remains of society.

graphic-violence: Shootings, brutal fights and a stabbing.

ratings: Violence, some sexuality, nudity and language

works.title: Moon
works.summary: Near the end of a three-year solo contract mining helium on the far side of the Moon, a lone worker starts to suspect his situation is not what he was told.

works.title: Coherence
works.summary: During a dinner party on the night a comet passes overhead, the power goes out and eight friends notice that the house down the street looks oddly familiar.

works.title: Primer
works.summary: Two engineers tinkering in a garage stumble on a side effect of their invention and must decide what to do with it.

works.title: Gattaca
works.summary: In a society that sorts people by their genes, a man conceived naturally assumes another's identity to pursue his dream of space travel.

graphic-violence: A murder investigation, with a brief violent image.

ratings: Brief violent images, language and some sexuality

works.title: Ex Machina
works.summary: A programmer is invited to a reclusive CEO's remote estate to assess whether the humanoid AI he has built is truly conscious.

graphic-violence: Sudden, bloody violence near the end.
A character is stabbed to death.

ratings: Graphic nudity, language, sexual references and some violence

works.title: Annihilation
works.summary: A biologist joins an expedition into a spreading, shimmering zone from which no previous team has returned.

graphic-violence: Creature attacks and shootings, with bloody and disturbing images.
body-horror: Disturbing bodily mutation, including a recorded scene of an open wound.
suicide-self-harm: A character takes their own life in recorded footage.
Kane kills himself with a phosphorus grenade on the expedition's video.

ratings: Violence, bloody images, language and some sexuality

works.title: Spirited Away
works.summary: A sullen ten-year-old wanders into a world of spirits and must work in a bathhouse for the gods to free herself and her parents.

jump-scares: Frightening spirits and transformations may scare young children.

works.title: My Neighbor Totoro
works.summary: Two sisters move to the countryside with their father and discover gentle forest spirits living nearby.

jump-scares: A short stretch of worry when a child goes missing.

works.title: Paddington 2
works.summary: A polite bear from Peru sets out to buy his aunt the perfect birthday present, and ends up wrongly accused of stealing it.

graphic-violence: Slapstick action and a train chase; nobody is hurt.

ratings: Some action and mild rude humor

works.title: Paterson
works.summary: A week in the life of a bus driver in Paterson, New Jersey, who writes poems in a notebook between shifts.

graphic-violence: A brief, tense confrontation in a bar.

works.title: Perfect Days
works.summary: A Tokyo public-toilet cleaner moves through his carefully ordered days of work, music, books and photographs of trees.

works.title: Columbus
works.summary: In a small Indiana town known for its modernist buildings, a young woman and a visiting man waiting on his ailing father strike up a friendship through architecture.

works.title: Parasite
works.summary: A struggling family schemes its way, one job at a time, into the employ of a wealthy household.

graphic-violence: A sudden, bloody outburst of violence late in the film.
sexual-content: A sexual scene without explicit nudity.

ratings: Language, some violence and sexual content

works.title: The Lives of Others
works.summary: In 1984 East Berlin, a Stasi officer assigned to bug a playwright's apartment becomes absorbed in the lives he is listening to.

suicide-self-harm: A suicide is a plot point and is discussed.
A blacklisted director hangs himself, which prompts the playwright's article.

works.title: Come and See
works.summary: A Belarusian teenager joins the partisans during the Nazi occupation and is plunged into the war's horror.

graphic-violence: Harrowing war violence against civilians.
atrocity: The massacre of a village's population is depicted at length.

works.title: Before Sunrise
works.summary: Two strangers meet on a train and spend one night walking and talking through Vienna before he must fly home.

works.title: Mad Max: Fury Road
works.summary: In a desert wasteland, a drifter and a rebel war rig driver flee a tyrant across the sands.

graphic-violence: Constant vehicular combat, shootings and disturbing images.

ratings: Intense sequences of violence throughout, and disturbing images

works.title: Story of Your Life

attributes.collected_in: Stories of Your Life and Others (2002)

works.summary: A linguist recounts learning the language of visiting aliens, and how it changed the way she experiences her own life.

works.title: Solaris
works.summary: A scientist arrives at a station above a planet covered by an ocean that may be a single vast mind, and that seems to be studying the researchers in return.

works.title: Roadside Picnic
works.summary: Years after a brief alien visitation left behind lethal, wondrous Zones, a hardened scavenger makes illegal runs to retrieve the artifacts inside.

works.title: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
works.summary: In a radiation-blighted San Francisco where owning a real animal is a status symbol, a bounty hunter pursues escaped androids.

works.title: Annihilation
works.summary: A biologist, one of four unnamed women on the twelfth expedition into Area X, keeps a journal of what they find.

works.title: The Left Hand of Darkness
works.summary: An envoy is sent to an icebound planet whose people have no fixed sex, to persuade its rival nations to join an interstellar alliance.

works.title: The Dispossessed
works.summary: A physicist from an anarchist moon colony travels to its capitalist mother planet, the first to cross between the two worlds in generations.

works.title: Piranesi
works.summary: A man lives contentedly in an endless house of marble halls and tidal seas, recording its wonders in his journals.

works.title: Never Let Me Go
works.summary: A woman looks back on her childhood at an English boarding school and the friendships that shaped her life.

sexual-content: Frank but non-graphic discussion of sex.

works.title: The Remains of the Day
works.summary: An aging English butler takes a motoring trip across the countryside and reflects on decades of service.

works.title: A Psalm for the Wild-Built
works.summary: A restless tea monk travels into the wilderness and meets a robot, the first seen by humans in centuries, which wants to know what people need.

works.title: Kindred
works.summary: A Black writer in 1976 Los Angeles is repeatedly pulled back in time to a Maryland plantation before the Civil War.

graphic-violence: Whippings, beatings and sexual violence under slavery are described.

works.title: Nineteen Eighty-Four
works.summary: A party functionary in a totalitarian superstate begins a secret diary and a forbidden love affair.

graphic-violence: Psychological and physical torture is described.

works.title: The Name of the Rose
works.summary: In 1327, a Franciscan friar and his novice investigate a series of deaths at a wealthy Italian abbey with a labyrinthine library.

works.title: Dune
works.summary: The heir of a noble house is drawn into a deadly struggle for control of a desert planet, the only source of the most valuable substance in the universe.

graphic-violence: Duels, assassinations and battles.

works.title: Outer Wilds
works.summary: A rookie astronaut sets out to explore a small, handcrafted solar system and its mysteries, with nothing but curiosity and a ship.

jump-scares: A few tense, frightening moments with deep-space creatures.

works.title: Disco Elysium
works.summary: An amnesiac detective wakes in a wrecked hotel room and must solve a murder while working out who he is, in a city still scarred by a failed revolution.

graphic-violence: Occasional violent encounters; a hanged body is examined in detail.
substance-use: Alcohol and drug use are central, and the player can choose to drink, smoke and take drugs.
suicide-self-harm: Suicidal thoughts and references to suicide.

works.title: Journey
works.summary: A robed traveller crosses a vast desert toward a distant mountain, sometimes accompanied by another player who cannot speak.

works.title: Hollow Knight
works.summary: A small, silent knight descends into a fallen insect kingdom of caverns and ruins.

graphic-violence: Constant combat with insect enemies; no blood.

works.title: Return of the Obra Dinn
works.summary: An insurance investigator boards a merchant ship that drifted back into port with its crew missing, and must account for the fate of every soul aboard.

graphic-violence: Many violent deaths, shown as frozen moments.

works.title: Papers, Please
works.summary: As a border inspector for a fictional Eastern Bloc state, you check documents, follow ever-changing rules, and try to keep your family fed.

graphic-violence: Terrorist attacks and shootings at the border, in pixel art.
sexual-content: Pixelated nudity from a body scanner.

works.title: Elden Ring
works.summary: A disgraced wanderer crosses a vast, broken land in search of the shards of a shattered ring of power.

works.title: SOMA
works.summary: A man wakes in an underwater research facility overrun by machines that seem to think they are human.

works.title: Kentucky Route Zero

attributes.release_note: Released episodically from 2013; year given is the complete edition

works.summary: A delivery driver searches for an address on a mysterious highway running beneath the caves of Kentucky.

works.title: Stardew Valley
works.summary: You leave an office job to take over your grandfather's overgrown farm and become part of a small valley town.

graphic-violence: Fighting monsters in the mines, without gore.
substance-use: Drinking at the saloon; one character struggles with alcohol.
suicide-self-harm: One optional storyline addresses depression and implied suicidal thoughts.

works.title: The Talos Principle
works.summary: An android wakes among ruins and is set a series of puzzles by a disembodied voice, while terminals hint at what happened to the world.

works.title: OK Computer
works.summary: Radiohead's third album: guitar music turned toward unease about technology, travel and modern life.

works.title: Ambient 1: Music for Airports
works.summary: Four slowly unfolding pieces of tape-loop music, intended to calm rather than demand attention.

works.title: Kind of Blue
works.summary: A sextet session built on spare modal frameworks, recorded largely in first takes.

works.title: Hounds of Love
works.summary: A side of ambitious art-pop singles followed by 'The Ninth Wave', a suite about a woman adrift alone in the sea at night.

works.title: In the Aeroplane Over the Sea
works.summary: Fuzzy, horn-laden folk songs, sung with raw intensity, haunted by love, death and history.

works.title: Discovery
works.summary: French house built from disco and soft-rock samples, nostalgic and euphoric.

works.title: Lift Your Skinny Fists Like Antennas to Heaven
works.summary: Four long instrumental movements that swell from quiet field recordings to roaring orchestral crescendos.

works.title: The Disintegration Loops
works.summary: Old tape loops that physically deteriorate as they play, recorded as they slowly crumble away.

relationships: Film adaptation of Ted Chiang's novella.
Loosely adapted from the Strugatskys' novel; the brothers wrote the screenplay.
Loose adaptation of Philip K. Dick's novel.
Loose adaptation of the first Southern Reach novel.
Direct sequel set thirty years later.
Solitary figures on remote stations confronting doubles and the unreliability of their own pasts.
Both reframe a life through knowledge of time and its ending.
Both ask what would make a machine mind a person.
Both test where machine personhood begins.
Ordinary functionaries inside a surveillance state, and the cost of complicity.
Wordless, meditative experiences built on slow-moving atmosphere.
Wonder-driven exploration of a vast, strange place, where understanding is the reward.
Beauty found in decay and things slowly passing.
Gentle portraits of a man's daily rituals and the poetry in routine.
Robots as gentle companions asking what humans need, against Dick's paranoid hunt.
An imperfect anarchist society set against a totalitarian one.
Both take political ideologies seriously and examine their failures.
